# Real-text corpora

The synthetic `cjk_4k` / `cjk_1m` workloads draw ideographs uniformly from
U+4E00-U+6DFF, which is adversarial rather than representative: most of what it
produces are rare characters that miss the vocabulary and fall through to the
byte-pair merge, at ~1.45 bytes/token on cl100k_base. Real CJK text is drawn
from a few thousand common characters and hits multi-character vocabulary
entries constantly. These files exist so the CJK result can be stated about real
text rather than about the generator.

| file | source | licence |
|---|---|---|
| `udhr_zho.txt`, `udhr_jpn.txt`, `udhr_kor.txt` | Universal Declaration of Human Rights, UDHR in Unicode corpus (`chn`, `jpn`, `kkn`), from the archive at <https://unicode.org/udhr>, which [`test/get_udhr.py`](../../test/get_udhr.py) also points at | UN document, free to reproduce |
| `hongloumeng.txt` | 紅樓夢 (Cao Xueqin, 18th c.), Project Gutenberg ebook 24264, a contiguous 256 KiB slice with the Gutenberg header and footer removed | public domain |

Sizes are natural, not padded: nothing here is a short text repeated to length,
so no measurement is reading a cache-resident loop.

Added for the same reason on the non-CJK side, since `prose_*` and `code_*` are
generated by drawing from a fixed fragment list and repeat far more than real
text does:

| file | source | licence |
|---|---|---|
| `mobydick.txt` | *Moby-Dick*, Melville 1851, Project Gutenberg ebook 2701, a contiguous 256 KiB slice past the front matter, header and footer removed | public domain |
| `gosrc.txt` | 256 KiB of Go standard library source (`net/http`, `encoding/json`, `os`, ...) from the local toolchain, non-test files, each preceded by its path | BSD-3-Clause, see [`GO-LICENSE`](GO-LICENSE) |

`gosrc.txt` keeps the per-file `Copyright ... The Go Authors` headers, and those
headers refer to a LICENSE file. BSD-3-Clause requires the conditions and the
disclaimer to travel with the source, so Go's licence is reproduced here as
[`GO-LICENSE`](GO-LICENSE) rather than left as a dangling reference.
